newsitem.title: GERMANY: German court says Iran ordered Berlin murders.
newsitem.headline: German court says Iran ordered Berlin murders.

text.p: A Berlin court said on Thursday that "Iran's political leadership" had ordered the 1992 assassination of a group of dissident Iranian Kurdish leaders in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant.

"Iran's political leadership ordered the crime," presiding judge Frithjof Kubsch said as he read out the court's opinion after handing down life sentences to the two main suspects, an Iranian and a Lebanese, in the case.
It was not immediately clear whether the opinion, which could take several hours to read out, would name which leaders the court thought were behind the gangland-style slaying.
Prosecutors in the trial infuriated Iran by alleging that Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenie ordered the killings and President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani approved them.
The Islamic state denies all responsibility for the killings and Bonn fears a sharp worsening of relations if the two leaders are named.
